about: Everyday human foods and whether dogs can have them. verdict: ok = fine in small plain amounts; careful = depends on amount/prep/dog; no = toxic or dangerous. General info only, not veterinary advice.

foods.name: Apple (slices)
foods.reason: Slices are fine. Remove the core and seeds.

foods.name: Banana
foods.reason: A few slices are fine. Sugary, so keep it small.

foods.name: Blueberries
foods.reason: Fine as a small treat.

foods.name: Strawberries
foods.reason: Fine in small amounts, cut up for small dogs.

foods.name: Watermelon (seedless flesh)
foods.reason: The flesh is fine. No rind, no seeds.

foods.name: Carrots
foods.reason: Raw or cooked, plain. Cut to a safe size.

foods.name: Green beans (plain)
foods.reason: Plain is fine. Casseroles often contain onion.

foods.name: Cucumber
foods.reason: Plain slices are fine. Not pickles (salt, sometimes onion/garlic).

foods.name: Plain pumpkin
foods.reason: Plain cooked or canned pumpkin is fine. Not pie filling.

foods.name: Sweet potato (plain, cooked)
foods.reason: Plain and cooked is fine. No butter, sugar or marshmallows.

foods.name: Potato (plain, cooked)
foods.reason: Cooked and plain only. Never raw or green potato.

foods.name: Rice (plain, cooked)
foods.reason: Plain cooked rice is fine.

foods.name: Chicken (plain, cooked, boneless)
foods.reason: Plain cooked boneless meat with no seasoning is fine.

foods.name: Turkey meat (plain, boneless, no skin)
foods.reason: Plain cooked white meat without skin is fine.

foods.name: Egg (cooked)
foods.reason: Fully cooked, plain egg is fine.

foods.name: Salmon / white fish (cooked, boneless)
foods.reason: Fully cooked and boneless only. Raw salmon can carry parasites.

foods.name: Popcorn (plain, air-popped)
foods.reason: Plain popped kernels only. No butter, salt or unpopped kernels.

foods.name: Peanut butter
foods.reason: Plain is fine in small amounts, but CHECK THE LABEL for xylitol (birch sugar), which is dangerous.

foods.name: Cheese
foods.reason: A small cube is okay for many dogs. Fatty, and some dogs don't handle dairy.

foods.name: Milk
foods.reason: Many dogs are lactose intolerant. A lick may be fine, a bowl may not.

foods.name: Plain yogurt
foods.reason: Plain, unsweetened, small amounts. Avoid sweetened or xylitol-containing kinds.

foods.name: Bread (baked, plain)
foods.reason: A small plain bite is fine. Watch for raisins, garlic or nuts in it.

foods.name: Ham / bacon
foods.reason: Very salty and fatty. Fatty foods can trigger pancreatitis. Best skipped.

foods.name: Turkey skin & drippings
foods.reason: Fatty; can upset tummies or trigger pancreatitis.

foods.name: Gravy
foods.reason: Fatty and salty, often contains onion or garlic.

foods.name: Mashed potatoes
foods.reason: Usually has butter, cream, salt, sometimes garlic. Set aside a plain spoonful instead.

foods.name: Cranberry sauce
foods.reason: Plain cranberries are okay; sauces are sugary and some mixes include grapes or raisins.

foods.name: Tomato (ripe fruit)
foods.reason: Ripe fruit in small amounts is generally fine. Leaves, stems and green tomatoes are not.

foods.name: Corn kernels (off the cob)
foods.reason: A few plain kernels are fine. The cob itself is a NO (blockage risk).

foods.name: Chocolate
foods.reason: Toxic. Dark and baking chocolate are the most dangerous.

foods.name: Xylitol / birch sugar (sugar-free gum, candy, some peanut butters)
foods.reason: Very dangerous even in small amounts. Check labels.

foods.name: Grapes, raisins, currants, sultanas
foods.reason: Can cause kidney failure, even in small amounts.

foods.name: Onions, garlic, leeks, chives
foods.reason: The onion family is toxic to dogs: raw, cooked or powdered.

foods.name: Macadamia nuts
foods.reason: Toxic to dogs.

foods.name: Cooked bones
foods.reason: Splinter and can injure mouth, throat and gut.

foods.name: Stuffing
foods.reason: Usually contains onion, garlic, and sometimes raisins.

foods.name: Raw yeast dough
foods.reason: Expands in the stomach and produces alcohol as it ferments.

foods.name: Alcohol
foods.reason: Toxic to dogs, even small amounts.

foods.name: Coffee, tea, energy drinks
foods.reason: Caffeine is toxic to dogs.

foods.name: Avocado
foods.reason: The pit is a choking/blockage hazard, and skin and leaves can upset dogs. Best avoided.

foods.name: Cherries (with pits)
foods.reason: Pits, stems and leaves contain cyanide compounds, and pits can block the gut.

foods.name: Pumpkin pie
foods.reason: Sugar, rich ingredients and spices like nutmeg. Plain pumpkin yes, pie no.

foods.name: Christmas pudding, fruitcake, mince pies
foods.reason: Packed with raisins, currants and often alcohol.

foods.name: Corn cob
foods.reason: A classic cause of intestinal blockage.

foods.name: Chips, pretzels, salty snacks
foods.reason: Too much salt is bad for dogs; flavored chips may include onion or garlic powder.

foods.name: Wild mushrooms
foods.reason: Some wild mushrooms are deadly. Plain store-bought ones are generally okay, but wild ones on walks are a vet call.

foods.name: Fat trimmings
foods.reason: Can trigger pancreatitis.

foods.name: Nutmeg
foods.reason: Toxic in larger amounts; common in holiday baking and eggnog.
